title: A Noetherian local Nagata domain has reduced completion
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local integral domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] which is a Nagata ring [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring]. Then its $\mathfrak m$-adic completion $\varprojlim_n A/\mathfrak m^n$ is reduced; equivalently $A$ is analytically unramified [def-weil-pbc-analytically-unramified].

proof.text: Induct on the finite Krull dimension $d=\dim A$: it is finite because the maximal ideal of a Noetherian local ring has finitely many generators and [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-dimension-le-generators] bounds its dimension by their number. If $d=0$, the only prime of the local domain $A$ is $(0)=\mathfrak m$, so $A$ is a field; its $\mathfrak m$-adic completion is $A$, which is reduced. In the inductive step assume the assertion for all Noetherian local Nagata domains of dimension strictly less than $d$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0331 (lemma-local-nagata-domain-analytically-unramified), first paragraph of proof, lines 45972-45975

proof.text: Let $S$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$. Since $A$ is Nagata, its quotient by $(0)$ is N-2 [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring], so $S$ is a finite $A$-module [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain]. It is a normal domain with fraction field $K$ [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal], and is Nagata [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-nagata-nagata]. Finiteness makes $S$ Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian] and integral over $A$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral], so $\dim S\le d$ [lem-weil-pbc-integral-extension-dimension]. The finite fibre $S/\mathfrak mS$ has finitely many maximal ideals by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-zero-dim-local-discrete-spectrum]; their preimages are exactly the finitely many maximal ideals $\mathfrak n_1,\ldots,\mathfrak n_r$ of $S$, since each contracts to $\mathfrak m$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-local-radical].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0331, proof, lines 45977-45985; Definition Tag 032R and Lemmas Tag 032T, 00OK (lemma-integral-sub-dim-equal)

proof.text: The inclusion $A\hookrightarrow S$ is an injection of finite $A$-modules, with finite cokernel because $A$ is Noetherian. Exactness of completion on finite modules [lem-weil-pbc-completion-exact-finite-modules] makes the induced ring map $\widehat A_{\mathfrak m}\hookrightarrow\widehat S_{\mathfrak mS}$ injective. Hence reducedness of the latter implies reducedness of $\widehat A_{\mathfrak m}$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0331, proof, lines 45986-45990; Lemma Tag 00MB (lemma-completion-flat), exactness of completion

proof.text: For each $n\ge1$, $A/\mathfrak m^n$ is Artinian local [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-quotient-artinian-local]. The finite algebra $B_n=S/\mathfrak m^nS$ over it has exactly the maximal ideals $\mathfrak n_i/\mathfrak m^nS$ and Jacobson radical consisting of nilpotent elements [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-zero-dim-local-discrete-spectrum]. The product decomposition [lem-weil-pbc-product-of-localizations-at-maximal], with each factor identified by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient], gives $B_n\cong\prod_i S_{\mathfrak n_i}/\mathfrak m^nS_{\mathfrak n_i}$, compatibly with reduction in $n$. Taking compatible inverse limits yields $\widehat S_{\mathfrak mS}\cong\prod_i\varprojlim_n S_{\mathfrak n_i}/\mathfrak m^nS_{\mathfrak n_i}$. Put $J=\bigcap_i\mathfrak n_i$. The ideal $J/\mathfrak mS$ is finitely generated, since $S/\mathfrak mS$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite] applies; each generator is nilpotent by the finite-fibre result, so a sufficiently high power of their ideal vanishes. Thus $J^N\subseteq\mathfrak mS$ for some $N$, whereas $\mathfrak mS\subseteq J$. On localization at $\mathfrak n_i$, distinct maximal ideals become the unit ideal, so $JS_{\mathfrak n_i}=\mathfrak n_iS_{\mathfrak n_i}$. Thus the powers of $\mathfrak mS_{\mathfrak n_i}$ and $\mathfrak n_iS_{\mathfrak n_i}$ are cofinal, and [lem-weil-pbc-change-ideal-completion] identifies each displayed inverse limit with $\widehat{S_{\mathfrak n_i}}_{\mathfrak n_i}$. Consequently $\widehat S_{\mathfrak mS}\cong\prod_i\widehat{S_{\mathfrak n_i}}_{\mathfrak n_i}$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0331, proof, lines 45983-45996; Lemma Tag 00DT (lemma-chinese-remainder) and Lemma Tag 0319 (lemma-change-ideal-completion)

proof.text: Each $S_{\mathfrak n_i}$ is a Noetherian local normal domain of dimension at most $d$ by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime], and is Nagata by [lem-weil-pbc-nagata-localization]. If its dimension is less than $d$, the induction hypothesis gives reduced completion. For factors of dimension $d$ it remains to prove the assertion for a normal local Nagata domain $R$ of dimension $d$; the argument in the next two steps does this. Products of reduced rings are reduced, so this proves reducedness of $\widehat S_{\mathfrak mS}$ and then, by step 3, of $\widehat A_{\mathfrak m}$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0331, proof, lines 45994-45999, reduction to the normal local case

proof.text: Let $(R,\mathfrak n)$ be a Noetherian normal local Nagata domain with $\dim R=d>0$. Choose $0\ne x\in\mathfrak n$. Since $xR=R\cap xR$ inside $\operatorname{Frac}(R)$, [lem-weil-pbc-normal-domain-fractional-principal-quotient-ass] says $R/xR$ has no embedded associated primes and every associated prime $\mathfrak p$ has height one. The localization $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a one-dimensional Noetherian normal local domain: normality comes from [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain], and its dimension is one by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime]. Hence it is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-dim-one-iff-normal]. This verifies conditions (2) and (3)(a) of [lem-weil-pbc-analytic-unramified-principal-criterion], while $x\ne0$ and $x\in\mathfrak n$ verify its condition (1).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0331, proof, lines 46000-46011; Lemma Tag 031T (lemma-normal-domain-intersection-localizations-height-1), clause (3) specialized to y=x, and Lemma Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr)

proof.text: For each associated prime $\mathfrak p$ above, $R/\mathfrak p$ is a Noetherian local domain and is Nagata by the quotient clause of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-nagata-nagata]. Its dimension is strictly less than $d$: any chain of primes above $\mathfrak p$ lifts to a chain in $R$, and prepending $(0)\subsetneq\mathfrak p$ lengthens it by one. The induction hypothesis therefore says $R/\mathfrak p$ is analytically unramified, verifying condition (3)(b). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-analytic-unramified-principal-criterion] with $t=x$ to obtain reducedness of $\widehat R_{\mathfrak n}$, completing the normal case and the induction.
